subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the derivative of sin 2x from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the definition you start from and the identity you use on the numerator.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. The definition itself earns it. Write the limit line before you touch any identity.

recall.must_convey: That the first principle f′(x) = lim(h → 0) [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h is written down with f(x) = sin 2x.
accept: start from the definition f of x plus h minus f of x over h
write the first principle limit as h tends to zero
take f of x as sin two x and substitute x plus h
first principle formula rasta, f of x plus h minus f of x by h
the derivative is the limit of the difference quotient

steps.why: The question names the method, so the definition is the thing being marked. Writing it costs one line and earns one mark even if the identity that follows slips.
common_mistakes: Using the chain rule and writing 2 cos 2x straight away, which earns nothing on a first-principle question.
steps.memory_tip: Every first-principle answer opens the same way: f(x + h) minus f(x), all over h.

steps.label: Use sin C − sin D
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Choosing the sum-to-product form is the decision the examiner looks for: it turns a difference of two sines into a product that has sin h in it.
lines: sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) sin((C−D)/2)
f′(x) = lim(h → 0) [2 cos(2x + h) sin h]/h

recall.must_convey: That sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C+D)/2) sin((C−D)/2) is applied with C = 2x + 2h and D = 2x, giving 2 cos(2x + h) sin h.
accept: use sin c minus sin d equals two cos half sum sin half difference
apply the sum to product formula to the two sines
the numerator becomes two cos of two x plus h times sin h
sin minus sin formula apply cheste two cos sin vasthundi
convert the difference of sines into a product

steps.why: The numerator is a difference of two sines. Sum-to-product turns it into a product, and only a product can be separated into a factor with an ordinary limit and a factor of the form sin h over h.
common_mistakes: Using sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2), which is the wrong member of the pair.
Halving only one of the two angles.
steps.memory_tip: sin minus sin puts the cosine outside and the sine inside: 2 cos(half sum) sin(half difference).

steps.label: Arrange sin h over h
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The standard limit applies only when the angle inside the sine equals the whole denominator. Here it already does, which is what makes sin 2x the shortest of the first-principle questions.
lines: The angle in sin h matches the h below it, so

recall.must_convey: That the product is separated so that (sin h)/h stands alone, and the standard limit (sin h)/h → 1 is named.
accept: separate sin h over h and use the standard limit
limit of sin h by h as h tends to zero is one
the angle inside the sine is already h so the limit applies
sin h by h standard limit one avuthundi
split the product and quote sin theta over theta equals one

steps.why: The product splits into a factor that is continuous at h = 0 and a factor that is the standard limit. Each can then be evaluated on its own.
common_mistakes: Cancelling sin h against h as though they were equal.
Multiplying by an extra 2 to make the angles match, when they already match.
steps.memory_tip: The standard limit needs the same angle above and below. Check the two agree before using it.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The 2 in front is the derivative of the inside angle 2x. It comes out of the sum-to-product step, not from anywhere else.
lines: As h → 0, cos(2x + h) → cos 2x and (sin h)/h → 1

accept: the answer is two cos two x
cos of two x plus h tends to cos two x so it is two cos two x
put h equal to zero and get two cos two x
answer two cos two x vasthundi
derivative of sin two x is two cos two x

steps.why: The remaining cosine factor is continuous, so its limit is its value at h = 0. The answer keeps the 2, which is what records that the inside angle was 2x and not x.
common_mistakes: Giving cos 2x and losing the factor 2.
Letting h → 0 inside sin h but not inside cos(2x + h).
steps.memory_tip: The number multiplying x inside the sine comes out in front: sin 2x gives 2 cos 2x.

insider_note: sin C − sin D turns the difference into 2cos(2x + h)sin h. Dividing by h gives sin h/h → 1, and the 2 in front is what makes the answer 2cos2x.
